subject: CTO briefing: buying criteria, procurement path & escalation items (Nimbus Health)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Javier Sanchez <javier.sanchez@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Angela Park <angela.park@nimbushealth.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + CTO briefing notes from today's call

Javier / Angela — thanks again for your time today. Quick post-call recap and the items we agreed to surface to your procurement and security teams. I wanted to make sure we captured the business outcomes and risk considerations correctly so we can align next steps.

Key business goals you shared:
- Reduce phone triage load by ~30% in Q4 by automating routine patient intake workflows (target: 100k tokens/mo pilot).
- Improve clinician turnaround on non-urgent messages (target 40% fewer manual escalations).
- Tight coupling with EHR alerts (read-only) — no PHI retention beyond 30 days in the service.

Primary pain / risk items from the call:
1) PHI handling and retention policy — Nimbus requires SOC 2 Type II, field-level encryption, and strict data residency controls.
2) Latency SLA — clinical workflows need <200ms median token latency for the inline triage flow.
3) Procurement/contracting timeline — committee meets every two weeks; goal is a POC kickoff within 6–8 weeks.

What Redwood can provide (summary):
- Pilot proposal: reserved capacity for a 100k token/month pilot using a quantized model variant; configurable KV cache and prefix caching to meet latency targets.
- Security pack: SOC 2 attestations, architecture diagram, and a summary of our data flow & retention controls (attached).
- Procurement-ready items: sample MSA, SOW template, and a simple pilot pricing worksheet.

Agreed next steps (owners & timeline):
- Redwood to send an exec-friendly briefing + security pack by EOD tomorrow (PR: me). Attachment: "20270804-nimbus-recap-deck.pdf" and security summary.
- Nimbus to send procurement intake form and list of required contractual clauses (owner: Angela).
- Schedule a focused engineering demo (latency + EHR integration pattern) in the next 7–10 days (owner: Marcus at Redwood).

Open questions we flagged to confirm:
- Final token retention window (you mentioned 30 days — please confirm whether that is strict or negotiable for the pilot).
- Pilot success metrics & decision criteria for full procurement (who signs off on pilot?).

Attachments: 20270804-nimbus-recap-deck.pdf (summary slides), security-briefing-exec-summary.pdf (SOC2 summary + data flow diagram).

Thanks — I'll loop in Marcus and Lauren internally to begin pricing and to coordinate the demo.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Javier Sanchez <javier.sanchez@nimbushealth.com>, Angela Park <angela.park@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + CTO briefing notes from today's call

Thanks for the crisp recap, Priyom — good capture. A couple of internal asks so we move cleanly: 

1) Pricing target: procurement will push for predictable unit economics. Can Marcus prepare two options for the pilot: (A) reserved monthly capacity (flat) and (B) usage-based with a token cap and overage rate. Include 1) estimated median latency for each, and 2) suggested billing cadence.

2) Contract redflags: Angela will likely request explicit language on data deletion and an audit right. Legal will want a short addendum for PHI handling during the pilot. Grace — please pull our SOC2 Type II cert and the most recent penetration test summary; add as an appendix to the security pack.

3) Escalation path: If Nimbus requires sub-200ms median latency, we should pre-agree on fallback routing (e.g., route to a lower-latency replica or a smaller context model) and include a SLA exception process. Marcus — can you draft an operational runbook for the pilot covering fallback behavior and monitoring alerts?

Once we have the two pricing options and security appendix, Priyom, send a single consolidated package to Javier and Angela. They asked for an exec-friendly brief for their committee — keep it one page for leadership and include the procurement ask.

I'll be available to join the demo; Marcus, coordinate times.

-Lauren
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (212) 555-0124

---

From: Javier Sanchez <javier.sanchez@nimbushealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Angela Park <angela.park@nimbushealth.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + CTO briefing notes from today's call

Priyom / Lauren — thanks for the follow-up and for being so thorough. A few clarifications from our side to speed procurement: 

- Confirmed: decision committee = CTO (me), Head of Clinical Ops (Dr. Rebecca Lane), Procurement lead (Angela). We meet every other Tues; next meeting is Aug 17. Target: pilot approval there to start kickoff the week of Aug 23.

- Security: SOC 2 Type II is required. We also need an architecture diagram that shows how Redwood handles ephemeral KV caches, where encryption occurs, and what logs (if any) are exported. The "security-briefing-exec-summary.pdf" looked good; can you add a one-page architecture diagram with call flow?

- PHI/data retention: Our default is strict: no managed retention beyond the session for any PHI fields. For the pilot, we can allow 30-day retention if there is a signed addendum with clear deletion triggers and auditability.

- Performance targets: For the inline triage flow we need median per-token latency under 200ms, and 95th percentile under 400ms. If you can provide historical telemetry for similar customers (median, p95) that will help our engineering review.

- Procurement asks: I'll upload our standard intake form (attached) and a list of contract clauses we prioritize (liability caps, data deletion, audit rights). Angela will follow up with a clean copy.

One more ask: can Redwood commit to a 30-day runbook for incident response during the pilot and a named escalation contact? We want to avoid surprises in clinical hours.

We'll review the consolidated brief ahead of our Aug 17 committee meeting. Appreciate a single packet from you by COB Mon Aug 9 if possible.

Thanks,
Javier Sanchez
CTO, Nimbus Health
javier.sanchez@nimbushealth.com | +1 (415) 555-0987

Quick internal note to confirm owners and immediate actions after Javier's clarifications below.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Security appendix + one-page architecture diagram (Grace) — deliver by Mon 2027-08-09 COB. Include SOC2 cert, pen test summary, and explicit data deletion flow. Attach: security-briefing-exec-summary.pdf (update).
- Pilot pricing options (Marcus) — two alternatives (reserved vs usage-based) + expected median/p95 telemetry examples — draft by Mon 2027-08-09 EOD.
- Operational runbook & SLA exception flow (Marcus + Grace) — include fallback routing, on-call escalation names, and 30-day incident response SLA. Draft by Tue 2027-08-10.

Marcus — estimate engineering delta for option A vs B in your pricing doc.

I'll schedule the demo with Marcus and attach the intake form once Angela uploads it.

Thanks team — close coordination this weekend will let us hit the Aug 9 delivery ask.

Priyom
